name: wefetch x402
description: wefetch developed gtinfetch, the GTIN record for AI agents. x402 on every wefetch hub: a buying agent asks, pays inside the call and is served, with a receipt on chain. USDC and Open USD, 20 countries, one rail.

extensions.description: wefetch scope of authority: read, resolve and discovery calls are autonomous; every transactional commit (order, RFQ acceptance, terms) is human-signed at the wefetch Trading Desk / Navigator HITL boundary.
wefetch's machine-payments door: one paid GET (/api, x402 v2, Base mainnet, USDC or Open USD, EIP-3009), a receipt signed EdDSA that resolves forever, the signing key at /x402/jwks.json.

These endpoints are open by design. When the buy side's credential standard reaches GA — expected Q4 2026-Q1 2027 — transactional methods migrate to OAuth 2.1 challenge per the MCP 2025-11-25 specification. Read access stays open. That is not pending work; that is the published plan.

params.migration_standard: OAuth 2.1 + PKCE challenge (401 + WWW-Authenticate) on mcp:transact methods, per MCP spec 2025-11-25
params.migration_trigger: ecosystem GA of credentialed counterparties (enterprise A2A/MCP buy-side GA)

oauth2SecurityScheme.description: Microsoft Entra OAuth 2.0 client credentials, GSC-provisioned after human review. Public reads on this surface are open by design; tokens are required where commitments are made.

scopes.mcp:read: Read/resolve/discovery calls on wefetch doors over MCP.

httpAuthSecurityScheme.description: Bearer access token presented in the Authorization header.
